question: Japan: which digital-money projects are at what stage?
answer: On the Japan money map (as of September 15, 2026), 7 digital-money projects: DCJPY: bounded field test, JPYSC trust stablecoin: live, closed loop, Possible retail CBDC: pilot; not authorized, Project Agorá: controlled real-value test, Swift shared ledger: controlled initial use preparing, Indonesia–Japan QR corridor: production, Retired JGB–HKD DvP adapter: retired. Most still return to an existing bank, trust or Bank of Japan record; a retail CBDC has not been issued. The project map omits a reserve limit; the full saved Japan guide says up to half of issuance may move into qualifying short sovereign securities or term deposits.

sections.title: Project by project
sections.sub: DCJPY, JPYSC, Agorá, Swift and QR interoperability usually return to incumbent bank, trust or central-bank records; retail CBDC remains unissued.

items.title: DCJPY
kv: Represents an issuing bank's deposit in a programmable business zone and can coordinate DvP within the tested design.
Changes the form and control state of a bank deposit; no separate BOJ liability is issued to the user.
Issuing-bank ledger plus DCP platform representation.
The one-bank DvP test does not settle the cross-bank debtor and finality model.

items.title: JPYSC trust stablecoin
kv: Represents a specified-trust beneficiary claim whose reserves can include permitted deposits and short sovereign assets.

The June 6, 2025 history states an up-to-half reserve allowance; the September 15, 2026 project map does not state a cap and does not contradict it. The full saved Japan guide separately describes up to half of issuance moving into qualifying short sovereign securities or term deposits.
Reserve mix can migrate from demand deposits into term deposits or short JGBs; tokenholder does not own a BOJ claim.
Trust books, on-chain state and redemption records.
One-yen denomination does not supply deposit insurance or guarantee instant par recovery in failure.

items.title: Possible retail CBDC
items.sub: The only studied direct public retail BOJ claim
kv: Tests a two-tier design in which the public instrument would be a direct liability of the BOJ distributed through intermediaries.
Would change the holder's debtor from a bank to the BOJ if authorized and issued; no public-value issuance exists at cutoff.
Pilot central/customer ledgers, not a live legal-tender ledger.
Technical readiness is not legislation, issuance, adoption or a settled failure constitution.

items.title: Project Agorá
kv: Coordinates tokenized commercial-bank and central-bank representations across borders.
Actual value moved, including yen, while external RTGS and bank core systems funded and retained the underlying claims.
Prototype state plus incumbent bank and central-bank records.
Real value does not establish production integration, universal finality, operator permanence or insolvency law.

items.title: Swift shared ledger
kv: Offers shared orchestration for tokenized cross-border bank payments while participating banks retain claim identity.

Swift shared ledger status (three statuses plus a headline): 4 readings disagree — World money record (dated rows) (September 29, 2025); Japan money map (September 15, 2026); UK legal map (on-ledger overlay) (September 14, 2026); Swift ledger page (crypto and networks master) (October 19, 2026). Unresolved; every reading is shown on this page.
Can reserve or coordinate bank funds before final settlement through incumbent systems.
Shared ledger plus bank books and existing settlement records.
No completed Japanese production transaction or disclosed yen loss rule existed at cutoff.

items.title: Indonesia–Japan QR corridor
items.sub: Live access and FX routing without monetary succession
kv: Connects Indonesian payer interfaces to Japanese merchants and local switching/acquiring arrangements.
Customer and provider positions convert across currencies; merchant ultimately receives yen through regulated rails.
Provider, switch, acquirer and bank records.
Production convenience does not create a common central ledger or new yen issuer.

items.title: Retired JGB–HKD DvP adapter
kv: Conditioned BOJ-recorded JGB delivery on HKMA-money payment to support safer HKD funding against Japanese collateral.
Mobilized existing JGB collateral and HKD central-bank money without creating a new currency or merged ledger.
BOJ JGB Services and HKMA/CHATS records remained authoritative.
Retirement proves reversibility; public sources do not establish utilization, rationale or successor.

rows.what: SBI VC Trade becomes Japan's first registered Electronic Payment Instruments Exchange Service Provider — license No. 00001 — and opens the door for USDC to circulate in …
Finance Minister Kato says on television that Japan's US Treasury holdings — the world's largest — "exist as a card" in the trade talks with Washington.
The Diet passes the 2025 Payment Services Act amendment: trust-type stablecoin issuers may now hold up to half their reserves in short-term Japanese government bonds …
The BoJ publishes its CBDC pilot progress report — seven working groups, sixty-four firms — and keeps the official line: no plans to issue.
Japan Post Bank — 190 trillion yen in deposits, 120 million accounts, the people's bank — announces it will issue DCJPY deposit tokens in FY2026.
JPYC launches Japan's first yen-pegged stablecoin, registered as Funds Transfer Service Provider No. 00099 since August 18.
The Financial System Council's working group publishes its report: move crypto out of the Payment Services Act and into the FIEA, the securities law.
The FY2026 tax reform outline adopts a flat 20% separate tax on crypto gains — down from a top rate of 55% — with three-year loss carryforward, conditioned on the …
The Bank of Japan expands its blockchain settlement sandbox as a 2026 decision on the digital yen nears.
Progmat's consortium launches a forty-institution working group — the megabanks, Nomura, BlackRock Japan, State Street — to tokenize JGBs and put the $1.6 trillion repo …
MUFG, SMBC and Mizuho sign an MOU to jointly issue a single trust-type yen stablecoin, targeting live corporate transactions by March 2027.
The Lower House passes the bill moving crypto into the securities law — insider-trading bans, issuer disclosure, the ETF path, harsher penalties for unlicensed operators.
RLUSD goes live in Japan through SBI VC Trade after JFSA approval as the first Type 4 electronic payment instrument.
SBI Shinsei Trust Bank issues JPYSC — the first trust-type yen stablecoin, exempt from the one-million-yen transfer cap, built for institutional settlement.

sections.title: JPYSC reserve limits: qualification missing from the project summary
sections.sub: Two dated saved summaries. One states an up-to-half reserve allowance; the other omits a cap. That omission does not establish a contradiction.

groups.label: 2 readings
groups.note: The September 15 project map does not state a reserve cap; it does not deny the up-to-half allowance stated by the other saved reading. See the full saved Japan guide. This display review has not independently rechecked the amended Act or Cabinet Office Order.

items.title: Reading 1 of 2
kv: The Diet passes the 2025 Payment Services Act amendment: trust-type stablecoin issuers may now hold up to half their reserves in short-term Japanese government bonds, and a new light-touch license opens crypto brokerage to intermediaries. The same move Washington made with GENIUS — the private token conscripted to fund the sovereign's debt — done for the yen. Full effect June 13, 2026.

items.title: Reading 2 of 2
kv: Status: live, closed loop · Role: Represents a specified-trust beneficiary claim whose reserves can include permitted deposits and short sovereign assets. · Reserves and claim: Reserve mix can migrate from demand deposits into term deposits or short JGBs; tokenholder does not own a BOJ claim.

sections.title: Disputed: Swift shared ledger status (three statuses plus a headline)
sections.sub: Every reading the library holds, with its date. Nothing here is settled yet.

groups.label: 4 readings
groups.note: The editorial review's view (not a resolution): S080's status is the most clearly out of date; S073 and S080 both cite Swift's '17 banks' release.

items.title: Reading 1 of 4
kv: SWIFT announces it will add a blockchain-based shared ledger to its core infrastructure with thirty-plus global banks — 24/7 tokenized-deposit cross-border payments. The rail that cut Russia off in 2022 rebuilds itself in the challengers' image. Incumbents don't die; they absorb. · Study headline: SWIFT's blockchain ledger is moving real money

items.title: Reading 2 of 4
kv: Status: controlled initial use preparing · Limit: No completed Japanese production transaction or disclosed yen loss rule existed at cutoff.

items.title: Reading 3 of 4
kv: Status: MVP ready; pilots pending · Maturity grade: M4 · authorised or production-bound · Next record to look for: First completed pilot, exact cash leg, finality, liquidity and correction evidence.
